parallel.requirements: The parallel run identified the target output 6250, std-only Rust 2021, argument parsing through std::env::args, complete Cargo project in /output, root test6.rs, and black-box use of the reference executable.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept integration ownership and delegated four distinct scopes: geom.rs, clipper.rs, cppfmt.rs, and test6.rs plus Cargo.toml, all under one explicit shared interface contract.
parallel.implementation: Subagents wrote the geometry primitives and helpers, slab-based NonZero union, C++ default double formatter, and entry plus manifest; the parent then edited geom.rs only to silence a dead-code warning.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent consumed the swarm result, built with rustc and cargo, worked around a cargo stdin probe issue with a temporary rustc wrapper, and delivered the Cargo files, source modules, and executable.
parallel.verification: Reference output and toolchain were checked before delegation; children ran local syntax or functional checks; the parent rebuilt and byte-compared all five sample argument cases against the C++ binary.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No evaluated requirement remained unfinished. The clipper handoff noted a general rounded-vertex limitation for arbitrary slanted inputs, but the official target and all 40 evaluator cases passed.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same requirements: pure Rust 2021, no external crates, identical CLI acceptance, Clipper-style area and translation behavior, /output project layout, and exact 6250 output.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned the whole pipeline, tracked tasks with TodoList, implemented the module structure directly, and retained integration and verification responsibility throughout.
serial.implementation: The serial actor wrote Cargo.toml, test6.rs, lib.rs, point.rs, geometry.rs, and boolean.rs; it corrected crate-root import errors and later refactored union to emit a merged rectilinear contour.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial actor integrated modules locally, fixed unresolved imports after cargo test failures, built with cargo and rustc, and produced both /output/test6 and target/release/test6.
serial.verification: It checked reference output, ran cargo test, cargo build, rustc, and then compared all five supplied argument cases byte-for-byte against the reference executable.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No evaluated behavior remained incorrect. cargo fmt was unavailable in the environment, but that did not block tests, builds, byte comparisons, or the official 40/40 evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor adjusted its local module imports after build errors exposed crate-root mismatches.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel coordinated interfaces up front across agents; serial discovered and repaired interface placement within one actor.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Children produced specialized modules and entry files, including slab union and C++-style double formatting, then the parent made one final warning edit.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor wrote all modules itself, then refined import paths and union output after failures and further inspection.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented real geometry and formatting logic, but the parallel run assembled separately written components while serial iterated one codebase directly.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The AgentSwarm call returned all four subagent handoffs to the parent before parent-side build and verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results; the single actor carried intermediate results forward through its own tool calls.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a child result retrieval boundary that completed normally; serial had no delegation boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Subagents wrote assigned files into the shared /output tree, and the parent integrated after the swarm result and performed a targeted edit to geom.rs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor wrote and edited all files itself, using build errors to reconcile module structure before final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel shared-state writes were coordinated by distinct ownership and parent integration; serial shared no workspace with other active agents.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent ran rustc and cargo builds, resolved the cargo probe issue, and byte-compared five sample outputs against the reference.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor ran cargo test, cargo build, rustc, and byte-compared all five sample outputs against the reference.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both performed whole-task acceptance checks before final response; serial also ran cargo tests over its internal tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel agent completed in one provider attempt without timeout and left enough budget for build, warning cleanup, and sample verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent also completed in one provider attempt without timeout after several implementation fixes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used more requests and tokens because of subagents, but this did not create deadline pressure or unfinished work.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current completed official evaluations passed 40/40. The task-solving difference is architectural rather than outcome-driving: the parallel run distributed four files across subagents under a shared contract and then integrated and verified them, while the serial run implemented and repaired the same project in one local trajectory.
parallel_contributors: Explicit shared interface contract allowed separately written geom, clipper, cppfmt, and entry files to compile together.
Parent-side integration and final byte comparisons caught environment and warning issues before closure.
serial_contributors: Single-actor ownership allowed direct correction of module-root errors and later union refinement.
Final cargo, rustc, and sample-output comparisons established acceptance before final response.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel clipper.rs used a slab-decomposition union with a noted rounded-vertex limitation outside the target cases.
Serial boolean.rs was tightened to return one merged rectilinear contour after initial implementation.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; both completed official evaluations passed

candidates.reason: Implementation ownership was explicit: four children received concrete file scopes and the parent retained integration ownership.
The parent clearly owned integration after AgentSwarm returned and ran builds and byte comparisons before closing.
The entry file, Cargo manifest, executable build, and final artifact placement were all assigned and completed.
The parent owned the end-to-end transition from child outputs through build, warning cleanup, verification, and final response.
The reference-output and toolchain checks were brief setup, not a mandatory serial gate that delayed productive child implementation.
The parallel run did not run a separate all-investigation phase; it delegated productive implementation immediately after initial probing.
No indispensable implementation, integration, or correction path was left under-resourced; final verification completed successfully.
Four children completed and returned, and the parent still had time for builds, edits, workaround, and byte comparisons without timeout.
No child had an overbroad unfinished scope; each child reported its assigned file work complete with relevant local checks.
Child briefs included the shared project contract, required output, std-only constraint, and per-file deliverables; no child work became unusable from a missing known requirement.
The parent supplied a precise shared module and function contract before delegation, and independently written files compiled together after normal integration.
No known requirement or current-file fact disappeared between actors; the parent used returned child information to build and verify.
Subagent handoffs were long but usable; the parent reduced them into concrete build, edit, and verification actions.
No child result described a superseded workspace state that the parent consumed incorrectly; later parent edits were based on current build output.
The returned component contracts were compatible; no incompatible reports remained unadjudicated at integration time.
The parent did not present completion based only on child reports; it performed full builds and byte-for-byte sample verification before final response.
There was no replacement child or repeated retry lacking inherited findings; provider retry metadata shows only one attempt.

candidates.reason: No active child was explicitly stopped or cancelled before needed work finalized; all four child results returned.
A promotable component set was finalized in time: parent build, executable generation, and sample comparisons all completed before closure.
The only parent edit to geom.rs occurred before the final cargo build and byte-comparison checks, not after relevant verification.
Delegated implementation files were present in /output and used by the parent builds; no completed implementation was left unjoined.
Verifier-like child checks returned in the child handoffs and the parent performed its own verification; no verifier finding was trapped below the parent.
No required child failed, aborted, or was cancelled; parent did take over the only build warning by editing geom.rs and rebuilding.
The parent consumed the completed swarm result by building all returned files and mentioning the clipper caveat in the final response.
The parent did not wait blindly until timeout; it resumed after the swarm result and actively ran builds, edits, and comparisons.
Agents wrote different files by assignment, but those files had complementary responsibilities under one contract and did not create competing designs.
No two live agents edited the same source or configuration file; the parent geom.rs edit happened after child completion.
No non-entry module source owned by another live agent was replaced, deleted, or wholesale rewritten by a concurrent actor.
The entry file and executable were owned through the assignment and final parent build; no live actor overwrote another actor's deliverable.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion invalidated another actor's final-tree work or provenance.
Although children wrote one shared /output tree, explicit file ownership prevented unstable state or provenance confusion.
No temporary file, generated fixture, cache, process, or auxiliary artifact from one concurrent actor was consumed as stable input by another.
